what_this_is: The largest Koblitz subgroup this repository's family offers, measured end to end, and the projection that follows for where the advantage runs out. K_0/F_2^53 has a 44-bit subgroup, 38 times the degree-41 rung.
the_laws: At a fixed memory budget the factor base is fixed, and then: the descent costs 2r/|F|^2 probes, so it grows linearly in r; relation collection costs about 9r/(n|F|) lookups, also linear in r; and rho costs sqrt(pi r/2)/sqrt(2n) steps, which grows as the square root. Linear loses to a square root, so rho overtakes — the question is only where.

projection.basis: the constants this run measured: 0.20 us a probe, 1.22 us a rho step, a 15264-point base

reading: The charged advantage survives to about a 52-bit subgroup and is gone by 53. The whole-process advantage dies sooner in practice: it needs a batch of targets that grows with r — 16 at 40 bits, 96 at 45, 315 at 48, 834 at 50 — because the precompute grows linearly while rho grows as a square root. What stops this is relation collection, not the descent.
what_this_is_not: Not a single-instance claim at any size. Even where the batch verdict holds, one target alone costs the whole precompute and rho wins.
Not a statement about the exponent: everything here is a constant at a fixed memory budget. A larger budget moves the boundary by half a bit per doubling of |F| and no more.
Not independent: one build, one host, one series.
The projection is arithmetic on two measured constants, not a series of runs. Where it is checked against this degree-53 run it under-predicts the win by about 1.7x.
